api_cases_detail.route_correction: Actual live route is GET /api/cases/:id keyed by thatcher's internal case id (e.g. mt2x82jm-aez37q2v), not :ref (CASE-1028-TWJXKSEV) as originally assumed in the task description -- ref is a display/lookup field, id is the store primary key store.getCase() takes.
api_cases_detail.note: Well under 200ms target on every attempt, worst-case included. Real case returned with full event history, transitions, report_fill_rate, suggested_assignee.

api_cases_update.route_correction: Actual live route is PATCH /api/cases/:id (not POST /api/cases/:ref/update as originally assumed) -- cases.js line 248, editable fields: subject/summary/priority/tags/assignee/autonomy/case_type.
api_cases_update.regression_note: 9/10 attempts pass (66.5-124.2ms, within 200ms target). Attempt 5 spiked to 267.3ms (33% over target) -- a single worst-case outlier, not a sustained trend (attempts 6-10 immediately returned to 66-73ms baseline). Root cause: PATCH does a real audited write (case row update + appended event with field-diff old/to for the changed summary field, per AGENTS.md's field-correction-is-distinguishable-from-first-fill invariant) plus optimistic-lock version check -- write path is inherently costlier than the pure-read detail endpoint (11.8ms mean), and one write in ten most likely hit a transient contention window (sqlite writer lock, or GC pause) rather than a structural defect. Worth a follow-up profiling pass if this recurs at higher write concurrency, but not remediated in this baseline session -- captured as observed, not fixed, per this row's scope (measurement only).

end_to_end_report.description: Time from contact message send to reply received (LLM-mediated agent turn, real channel)
end_to_end_report.reason: No LLM provider credentials are configured in this dev .env (CASEY_LLM_MODEL=auto but no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ACPTOAPI-reachable provider). GET /api/health confirms this live: {"ok":false,"label":"AI helper: offline","source":"none","model":null,"degraded":false}. AGENTS.md's own no-mocks invariant ('a degraded turn never fabricates case content and never claims to have understood the report') forbids synthesizing a fake reply to produce a number here -- doing so would violate the same design principle this baseline is meant to protect. Discord channel IS live and connected (gateway.channels.discord: {state:'ok', connected:true, sinceConnectMs:131522}) but posting a real message to a real Discord server crosses this session's world-scope boundary (reaching another party) without explicit user authorization.

case_sweep_cycle.description: Time to detect coverage gap / case-health breaches and page the team
case_sweep_cycle.distinction: Two different quantities exist under this name: (a) the SCHEDULING INTERVAL between sweep passes (config value, default 900000ms/15min, CASEY_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS unset in this .env so default applies) -- not something to 'measure' as a latency, it is a poll period; (b) the DETECTION LATENCY of one sweep pass itself (how long the scan+classify+tag+notify work takes once it runs) -- this is the real, measurable quantity, captured below from the live system's own last real sweep.

live_sweep_state.source: GET /api/health/cases (real authenticated call against the running instance)

detection_query_latency.endpoint: GET /api/health/cases (reads the already-persisted sweep result -- a proxy for the classification-read cost, not the full scan-and-tag write cost of a fresh sweep pass)

case_sweep_cycle.caveat: sweepCases()'s own full scan-and-tag execution time (the actual write-path cost of one pass, scanning all 23 open cases and appending observation events for any newly-entered breach) was not independently re-run in-process this session -- doing so would require a second thatcher store handle against the live db.sqlite (a second cwd-bound sqlite connection risks lock contention against the running production-like process per AGENTS.md's documented Windows file-lock behavior), which this session judged unsafe to open against a live, other-sessions-touching instance without explicit need. The 23-case scan already completed once (last_run_at above, ~53 min before this measurement) with errors:0, confirming the pipeline itself works end-to-end on real data; its last real duration was not separately timestamped by the product code (sweepCases does not currently record its own start/end wall-clock, only last_run_at). Team coverage-gap paging (detectCoverageGap rising-edge alert) was not triggered/witnessed this session -- no roster+zero-reply-in-window condition was constructed, since forcing one would mean intentionally paging a real alert channel, another world-scope action requiring authorization.

api_responsiveness_read_paths.finding: Pure-read endpoints (dashboard root, case detail) stay well under target at all percentiles: root 7-17ms (vs 2000ms LCP budget), case detail 8.7-18.8ms (vs 200ms budget). The original file's unauthenticated-401 timings (2.6-5.6ms) were NOT representative of real handler cost -- they measured only the auth-rejection fast path, understating true authenticated latency by roughly one to two orders of magnitude depending on endpoint.
api_responsiveness_read_paths.implication: Read-path performance is not a concern at current data volume (23 cases). Re-baseline case-list/detail timing if case volume grows past low hundreds -- no pagination-cost data exists yet at that scale.

api_health_provider_target_miss.finding: Authenticated GET /api/health/provider: mean 74.14ms, worst-case 120.88ms against a 50ms target -- worst-case is 141% over budget.
api_health_provider_target_miss.root_cause: Route composes multiple live reads per call (llmStatus(), queueStatus(), gateway channel connection state, session/cookie verification) with no caching; each sub-read adds real latency that the original 401-shortcut measurement never touched.
api_health_provider_target_miss.recommendation: If 50ms is a hard SLA, consider caching llmStatus()/queueStatus() with a short TTL (seconds, not minutes, so degraded-state visibility is not delayed) or restructure a pure /api/health/provider/lite endpoint for high-frequency polling. Not remediated in this session -- out of scope for a measurement-only PRD row.

api_cases_update_tail_latency.finding: PATCH /api/cases/:id: 9/10 attempts within the 200ms target (66.5-124.2ms), 1/10 spiked to 267.3ms.
api_cases_update_tail_latency.root_cause: Not isolated in this session (see api_cases_update.regression_note) -- plausibly transient sqlite writer contention or GC, since surrounding attempts returned immediately to baseline with no gradual degradation.
api_cases_update_tail_latency.recommendation: Re-run this specific series (n=30+) in a dedicated follow-up to determine if the outlier rate is statistically consistent (systemic tail latency) or a one-off; not conclusive from n=10.
